claims.text: Place Dalida is a quiet little square tucked away at the L-shaped intersection of Rue Girardon and Rue de l'Abreuvoir.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The city of Paris officially created the square in 1996 to honour the beloved Italian-French singer Dalida, who lived in this very neighbourhood.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: To mark the 10th anniversary of her death in 1997, a beautiful bronze bust of the singer was added to the center of the square.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Sculpted by the French artist Aslan, the bust rests proudly atop five blocks of solid cut granite beneath the shade of three trees.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: An engraved plaque directly underneath the bust displays her real birth name, Yolanda Gigliotti, alongside her birth and death years: 1933–1987.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Today, it remains a surprisingly popular pilgrimage site where countless fans and tourists come to peacefully pay their respects.
claims.subject: self
